etymologies.etymologyHTML: From expose +‎ -ure.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The condition of being exposed, uncovered, or unprotected.

quote.citation: 2013 June 8, “Obama goes troll-hunting”, in The Economist, volume 407, number 8839, page 55:
quote.text: The solitary, lumbering trolls of Scandinavian mythology would sometimes be turned to stone by exposure to sunlight. Barack Obama is hoping that several measures announced on June 4th will have a similarly paralysing effect on their modern incarnation, the patent troll.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) Lack of protection from weather or the elements.

quote.citation: 1993, Paul Chadwick, The Ugly Boy, Dark Horse Books:
quote.text: As all of you know, a great tragedy occurred yesterday. Arthur Harcourt died of exposure sometimes in the morning in the woods off Mount Tom Road.

definitions.definition: The act of exposing something, such as a scandal.
The act or condition of being at risk of financial losses.
(countable, uncountable) That part which is facing or exposed to something, e.g. the sun, weather, sky, or a view.
(photography) An instance of taking a photograph.
(photography) The piece of film exposed to light.
(photography) Details of the time and f-number used.
(horticulture) The amount of sun, wind etc. experienced by a particular site.
